questions.question: Which Indian classical dance is distinguished by elaborately colourful makeup and unique face masks reflecting age-old martial arts prevalent in the state of Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kathakali is a classical Indian dance form which is a story play genre of art is the folk dance form of Kerala.
 
• It is distinguished by elaborately colourful makeup and** unique face masks **reflecting age-old** martial arts**.
 
• It is a combination of 5 forms of fine art which are –
 
 
• Natyam (expressions)
 
• Nritham (dance)
 
• Nrithyam (enactment) 
 
• Sangeetam (music)
 
• Vadya (instruments)
 
 
 
• Various costumes of characters of Kathakali –
 
 
• Sathwika (Hero)
 
• Katti (Villain)
 
• Minukku (females)
 
• Thathi (other characters)
 
 
 
• Types of Drums used in Kathakali – Maddalam, Chenda, and Idakka
 
• Kathakali is the most difficult style of the traditional dance form in which **actors speak ‘sign language’ **where **hand gestures are used to dictate word** part of the character and **facial and eye movements express emotions** and mood.
 
• Kathakali is performed on themes based on the epics of Ramayana and Mahabharata.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following is a complex permanent plant tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Complex Permanent Tissue: A **cluster of structurally distinct cells** carrying out a common function or series of functions is referred to as complex permanent tissue. They are **composed of various cell types**. 
 
• Phloem and xylem are **examples** of these tissues. 
 
 
• Xylem:
 
 
• It facilitates the movement of water and dissolved materials throughout the plant.
 
• The various parts of the xylem consist of **parenchyma**, vessels, tracheids, and xylem fibers.
 
• **Lignin **makes up the xylem fibers and **cheids**, which give the plant structural support.
 
 
 
• Phloem:
 
 
• Food particles can be transported with the help of phloem.
 
• Complementary cells, sieve cells, sieve tubes, phloem fibers, and phloem parenchyma make up phloem.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Permanent tissues: Although these cells can no longer spread, they are specialized to provide the plant with strength, elasticity, and flexibility.

 
 
• These tissues also fall into the following categories:
 
 
• Simple Permanent Tissue
 
• Complex Permanent Tissue​​
 
 
 
 
 
• Collenchyma: These are live, **elongated cells** with minuscule spaces between them.
 
 
• **Pectin **and **cellulose **make up their cell walls.
 
• It provides plants with mechanical support and a flexible structural framework.
 
• It is **found on the margins of leaves** and **stems**.
 
 
 
• Plants have an **apical meristem**, an area of cells that can divide and **expand at the terminals of their roots and shoots**.
 
 
• The apical meristems extend the roots and shoots and **give rise to the main body of the plant**.
 
• Because this and other meristems can divide indefinitely, unlike most mammals, plants can grow for the entirety of their lives.
 
 
 
• **Lateral meristems** : This kind of meristem is found along the stem and root's longitudinal axis.
 
 
• Another name for it is a **secondary meristem.**
 
• Through division, the lateral meristem's cells proliferate and aid in the **thickening of the stem and root**.
 
• One kind of lateral meristem that creates the xylem and phloem is the **vascular cambium**.

questions.question: Which state government has introduced India's first elephant death audit framework?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu **has launched the "**Tamil Nadu Elephant Death Audit Framework**," a **first-of-its-kind project in India**, to better account for elephant fatalities by documenting their causes.
 
• At the State Wildlife Board meeting, **Chief Minister MK Stalin** made this announcement.
 
• The framework aims to achieve **three key goals**:
 
 
• firstly, it provides a systematic standard protocol for conducting post-mortems to identify the cause(s) of elephant deaths;
 
• secondly, it investigates and analyzes the circumstances surrounding elephant deaths that could have been prevented; and
 
• thirdly, it develops corrective measures to prevent unnatural and preventive deaths by conducting periodic death audits and tracking these over time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Elephants in India**: According to **Project Elephant's 2017 census**, India is home to an **estimated 29,964 wild Asian elephants**, making it the **country with the highest population.**

 
 
• Approximately **60% of the species' global population** consists of it.
 
• **Karnataka **has the **highest number of elephants**, followed by Assam and Kerala.
 
 
 
• The **Indian Wild Life Protection Act of 1972** designates elephants as National Heritage animals and provides them with protection under the **Schedule** **I species.**
 
 
• With the primary goal of restoring elephant habitats and mitigating the suffering of elephants and the human population, the Indian government initiated "**Project Elephant" in 1991–1992**, a **Ministry of Environment, Forests & Climate Change** centrally sponsored scheme.
 
• Its goals included addressing the issue of human-animal conflict and offering financial and technical support to the Indian states that make up the elephant range in order to **safeguard the elephants**, their habitats, and their corridors.
 
• It also aimed to advance the welfare of elephants kept in captivity.
 
• The following** goals guided** the** launch of Project Elephant** (PE): 
 
 
• To protect elephants, their habitat & corridors
 
• To address issues of man-animal conflict
 
• Welfare of captive elephants

questions.question: Which country introduced the game of cricket?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**England**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The earliest documented mention of **cricket **is from the middle of the **16th century,** and it comes from **South East England**.
 
• With the first international matches played in the second half of the 19th century, it spread throughout the world along with the British Empire's expansion.
 
• In cricket,** two teams of eleven players** compete in a **bat-and-ball match** on a field that has a** 22-yard (20-meter) pitch** in the middle.
 
• Each team's wicket is made up of two bails balanced on three stumps.
 
• One member of the fielding team, the **bowler**, bowls the ball towards the striker's wicket from the other end of the pitch while two members of the **batting **team, the striker and nonstriker, stand in front of either wicket.
 
• In order for the batting team to score one run for each exchange, the striker's objective is to hit the bowled ball and then trade places with the nonstriker. Additionally, runs are counted when the ball is bowled or reaches or crosses the field's boundary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A**** **glossary of cricket terms:

 
 

 Terms
 Explanation
 
 

 Leg-Before Wicket (LBW)
 It's a way to get the batter out. In other words, the hitter is out if the umpire determines that the ball struck any portion of the batter's body—typically the leg—prior to striking the bat or missing the bat and would have struck the stumps.
 
 

 Maiden
 An over where no runs that are attributable to the bowler are scored (byes or leg-byes may be scored in this over, though, as these don't count against the bowler).
 
 

 Wide Ball
 A delivery that pitches too far away from the batsman and so proves impossible to score off. The umpire will single this by stretching his arms out horizontally; an extra will be added to the total and the ball will be bowled again.
 
 

 Bouncer
 A short-pitched ball which passes the batsman at chest or head height
 
 

 Chinaman
 A ball bowled by a left-arm slow bowler that turns into the right-hand batsman, in effect a left-arm legspinner. Named after Puss Achong.
 
 

 Mankad
 A term popular mainly in indoor cricket - but also fairly popular in Australia for outdoor cricket. Mankad is when the bowler brings his arm around and, instead of releasing the ball, runs out the non-striker by whipping off the bails. This type of dismissal is rare - and usually a warning is given to the batsman beforehand. Named after Vinod Mankad, who twice dismissed Australian Bill Brown this way.
 
 

 Doosra
 A Hindi/Urdu word which means "second" or "other", the doosra is the offspinner's version of the googly, delivered out of the back of the hand and turning away from the right-hand batsman.

questions.question: Who among the following led the Chittagong Armoury Raid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surya Sen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Chittagong Uprising**, also known as the **Chittagong Armoury Raid** by the British, was an attempt on **April 18, 1930**, by armed Indian independence activists** led by Surya Sen** to seize the police and auxiliary forces' armory from the Chittagong armoury in Bengal Province in British India (now in Bangladesh).
 
• The raiders belonged to the revolutionary** Indian Republican Army**, a group that supported armed rebellions as a way to free India from British colonial control.
 
• The group included **Ganesh Ghosh**, **Lokenath Bal**, **Ambika Chakrobarty**, **Harigopal Bal (Tegra)**, **Ananta Singh**, **Anand Prasad Gupta** etc.
 
• **Surya Sen**'s nickname, **Master Da**, came from his work as a **school teacher** .
 
 
• In 1916, while pursuing his B.A. at **Berhampore College (now MES College)**, he was impacted by nationalist ideas.
 
• He was chosen to **lead the Chittagong branch of the Indian National Congress in 1918.**
 
• He actively participated in the Non-Cooperation movement before being detained and held captive for two years, from 1926 to 1928, due to his revolutionary actions.
 
• Sen, a visionary and ebullient organizer, often quipped, "**Humanism is a special virtue of a revolutionary**."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​​​Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

 
 
• He was an Indian politician who held the positions of first Deputy Prime Minister and first Home Minister
 
• In addition to being an active member of the Indian National Congress, he practiced law. His birthdate was never officially documented. However, according to his matriculation exam documents, he was born on October 31, 1875.
 
• He was born in Gujarat, in Nadiad. Jhaverbhai Patel was his father, and Ladba was his mother. Siblings of Vallabhbhai Patel numbered five.
 
• He was often called Sardar.
 
• He was also called an Indian Bismarck.
 
• He was appointed as the President of the Indian National Congress during the Karachi session in 1931 
 
 
 
• Rabindranath Tagore:
 
 
• Bengali polymath Rabindranath Tagore (7 May 1861 – 7 August 1941) was involved in the Bengal Renaissance.
 
• He was a poet, novelist, playwright, composer, philosopher, social reformer, educator, and painter.
 
• Using Contextual Modernism in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, he transformed Indian art and music as well as Bengali literature.
 
• In 1913, he became the first non-European and the first lyricist to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature in recognition of his work Geetanjali.
 
• In the 1915, King George V bestowed upon Tagore a knighthood, which he later renounced following the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• While Tagore's graceful prose and enchanted poetry were immensely well-liked throughout the Indian subcontinent, his poetic songs were perceived as mystical and mercurial.
 
• He was a fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society.
 
• Tagore was referred as "the Bard of Bengal" and went by the monikers Gurudeb, Kobiguru, and Biswokobi.
 
• Geetanjali, Sadhana, Ghare-Baire, Gora and Rabindra Sangeet are among his important works.
 
• His works, "Jana Gana Mana" in India and "Amar Shonar Bangla" in Bangladesh, were selected as national anthems by two countries. West Bengal has made "Banglar Mati Banglar Jol" into its official state anthem.
 
• In 1901 he founded the famous Shantiniketan which later came to be known as Vishwabharati University.
 
 
 
• **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar:**
 
 
• **​**He is also known as** ****Veer Savarkar**.
 
• He was born on **28th May,1883 **in **Bhagur**, a village near **Nashik **in Maharashtra.
 
• He founded a secret society called **Abhinav Bharat Society**.
 
• He went to the United Kingdom and was involved with organizations such as **India House** and the **Free India Society**.
 
• He was the **president **of **Hindu Mahasabha** from **1937 to 1943**.
 
• Savarkar wrote a **book **titled ‘**The History of the War of Indian Independence**’ in which he wrote **about **the guerilla warfare tricks used in **1857 Sepoy Mutiny**.
 
• He also wrote the **book **‘**Hindutva: who is hindu?**’.
 
• He was **arrested **in **1909 **on charges of plotting an armed revolt against the **Morley-Minto reform (Indian Councils Act 1909)** and was convicted and sentenced to **50-years imprisonment** also known as** Kala Pani **and** transported in 1911 to the Cellular Jail in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the Graded Response Action Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To control air pollution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)**:

 
 
• GRAP is a series of **emergency protocols that take effect in the Delhi-NCR region after air quality hits a certain threshold** in order to stop further deterioration.
 
• Following the Supreme Court's ruling in the **2016 case of M. C. Mehta v. Union of India**, it was approved by the court in 2016 and made public in 2017.
 
• The GRAP is being **implemented **by the **CAQM ( Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR & Adjoining Areas) **starting in **2021**.
 
• Up to 2020, states were required to implement GRAP measures by the **Environment Pollution (Prevention & Control) Authority (EPCA)**, which was appointed by the Supreme Court.
 
• In 2020, the EPCA was abolished, and the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) took its place.
 
• The Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) provide meteorological forecasts and air quality data, respectively, that are used by CAQM.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Air Pollution** : It is the term used to describe the presence of compounds in the atmosphere that are detrimental to materials, the environment, or the health of humans and other living things.

 
 
• There are several distinct kinds of air pollutants, including particles (both organic and inorganic), **gases** (including ammonia, **carbon monoxide**, **sulfur dioxide**, **nitrous oxides**, **methane**, **carbon dioxide**, and **chlorofluorocarbons**), and living molecules.
 
 
 
• **Status of Air Pollution in India**:
 
 
• **India **ranked **seventh **in the world for air pollution in **2022**, and **Delhi **was the **most polluted capital city** for the fourth year in a row, according to **IQAir's World Air Quality Report**.
 
• The survey also revealed that 39 of the world's 50 most polluted cities were in India, with Ghaziabad and Bhiwadi at the top of the list.
 
• Data on **PM2.5** air quality from more than 30,000 ground-based monitors across 131 countries were utilized in the paper.
 
 
• **Fine particulate matter, or PM 2.5**, can pose a major health risk when breathed in.

questions.question: White light is composed of how many colours?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the 1660s, English physicist and mathematician** Isaac Newton** began a series of experiments with sunlight and prisms.
 
• He demonstrated that clear **white light was composed of seven visible colors**.
 
• One of the greatest scientific **books **ever written, **Opticks**, details** Newton's findings from his experiments using prisms** to bend light.
 
• He named the **hues that comprise the visible spectrum**: **red**, **orange**, **yellow**, **green**, **blue**, **indigo**, and **violet**, or **ROYGBIV**.
 
• The small range of the electromagnetic spectrum that is visible to the human eye is known as the **visible spectrum**.
 
 
• Typically, the human eye can detect wavelengths from **380 to 700 nanometers.**
 
 
 
• Radio, gamma, and microwave radiation are additional types of **electromagnetic radiation**—energy waves that are invisible to the human eye.
 
• **Cone cells**, which are located in human eyes, are sensitive to wavelengths in the visible range. They **make it possible for us to see every hue in the rainbow.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phenomenon of splitting light into its constituent colors is called **dispersion of light**.
 
• The bending of light as it moves from one transparent substance into another is known as **refraction**.

questions.question: The southern part of India lies within the _________ zone.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **southern part of India** lies within the **Tropical zone.**
 
• The** areas of Earth that surround the equator **are known as the **tropics**.
 
 
• The **Tropic of Cancer** in the **Northern Hemisphere**, located at** 23°26′10.2° (or 23.43616°) N**, and the **Tropic of Capricorn** in the **Southern Hemisphere**, located at **23°26′10.2° (or 23.43616°) S**, define their latitude.
 
• The **tropical zone** and the** torrid zone** are other names for the tropics.
 
• The tropics constitute 39.8% of Earth's surface area and contain 36% of Earth's landmass.
 
 
 
• The Tropic of Cancer cuts India into two parts : Northern India and Southern India. The southern part comes under Tropical zone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The locations with mild temperatures that fall between the polar and subtropical zones are known as** temperate zones.**

 
 
• The term "temperate zones" refers to the two **areas between the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle** and the Tropic of Capricorn and the Antarctic Circle.
 
• The** south temperate zone** is located **between the Tropic of Capricorn at 23° 27′ S and the Antarctic Circle at 66° 33′ S.**
 
• The** north temperate zone** is located **between the Arctic Circle at 66° 33′ N and the Tropic of Cancer at 23° 27′ N**.
 
 
 
• The areas of Earth that round its geographic poles—the North and South Poles—and are contained inside the polar circles are known as the **polar regions**, sometimes known as the **frigid zones** or **polar zones.**
 
 
• The **Antarctic ice sheet**, which covers most of Antarctica and the Southern Ocean in the south, and the floating sea ice that covers much of the Arctic Ocean in the north are the main features of these high latitudes.

questions.question: M.S. Gopalakrishnan mastered both Carnatic and Hindustani Classical music. He was a _________ maestro.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Violin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M.S. Gopalakrishnan**, sometimes known as **MSG**, was a Carnatic musician who lived from 10 June 1931 to 3 January 2013.

questions.question: Guru Nanak Jayanti is observed annually on the full moon date of which month in the Hindu calendar?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The celebration of** Gurpurab**, also called** Prakash Utsav**, honors the **birth of Guru Nanak**, the first Sikh guru.
 
• It is **celebrated **on the **Full Moon Day (Pooranmashi or Purnima)** of the** Lunar Month** of **Kartik**.
 
• **Guru Nanak**, the **founder of Sikhism** and one of the most well-known and significant Sikh gurus, is held in the highest regard by the Sikh people.
 
• One of the holiest holidays in Sikhism is this one. The **anniversaries of the ten Sikh Gurus** serve as the focal point of Sikh celebrations.
 
 
• The Gurus were in charge of forming the Sikhs' beliefs. The **Sikhs celebrate their birthdays**, known as **Gurpurab**, with prayers and festivities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Nanak** : The **first Guru and founder of Sikhism**, **Guru Nanak Dev Ji**, was born in the **Punjab **region of the Indian subcontinent in the village of **Talwandi **in **1469**. Located close to Lahore in modern-day Pakistan, the village is currently called **Nankana Sahib**.

 
 
• **Mehta Kalu ji**, the **father **of Guru Nanak Dev ji, worked as a local accountant. It was said about his **mother**, **Mata Tripta ji**, that she was a modest and deeply pious person.
 
• In his early twenties, Nanak moved to Sultanpur, an important town on the main road between Lahore and Delhi, where he worked as a clerk in the Lodi administration.
 
• When he was **about thirty years old**, he had an experience that he described as a revelation—a **direct encounter with God** that shaped the rest of his life.
 
• The** stories** Sikhs later told **about Guru Nanak**, called **janam sakhis**, recount his childhood inwardness along with his engagement with social issues.

questions.question: The average salinity of the oceans is _______ parts per thousand.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**35**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **average salinity of seawater **is about **35 grams per kilogram (g/kg) **of seawater, or** 35 ppt**.
 
• Seawater generally ranges from 33 ppt to 38 ppt. **Freshwater **lakes, rivers, and streams contain some dissolved matter—**1 ppt or less**.
 
• **Brackish water** is a mixture of fresh water and seawater, **below approximately 33 ppt**.
 
• **Hypersaline water**, or **brine**, is very salty seawater,** above approximately 38 ppt**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salinity**, which is **measured in parts per thousand (ppt)**, is the **amount of salt in grams per kilogram of saltwater**.

 
 
• The number of parts, or grams, of salt there are per thousand parts, or kilogram (1,000 g), of seawater is known as parts per thousand.
 
• The term "parts per thousand" (ppt) is frequently used. 
 
• Both **temperature **and **salinity** **affect density**.
 
• A **hydrometer **can be used to **determine the density of a liquid** by measuring the level at which the hydrometer floats in it.

questions.question: According to the Indian constitution, who is the head of the Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **President **of India is the **head of the Union** according to our constitution.
 
• He is the country's chief executive.
 
• He is elected by electoral college with a single transferable vote, in compliance with the proportional representation system as per Article 55(3).
 
• He serves a five-year term in office.
 
• The qualifications of the President are:
 
 
• Should be **Citizen of India**.
 
• Minimum age of **35 years**.
 
• Should meet the requirements to be eligible for election to the Lok Sabha.
 
• Should not occupy any office of profit within the national government, a state government, or any other public body.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Prime Minister of India is the head of the government at the centre.

 
 
• Under Article 75, he/she is appointed by the president of India if he/she has the confidence of the majority of Lok Sabha members.
 
• He can recommend a person's name for the post of Governor to the President.
 
• Article 74(1) states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with a Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.
 
 
 
• Chief Justice of India (CJI):
 
 
• Under clause (2) of Article 124 of the Constitution, the President of India appoints the CJI.
 
• The seniormost Supreme Court judge deemed eligible to serve as the CJI shall be appointed to the position.
 
 
 
• Article 71 of the Constitution of India deals with "Matters relating to, or connected with, the election of a President or Vice-President".
 
 
• According to Article 66, The Vice-President of India is elected by an Electoral College consisting of the members(elected and nominated) of both Houses of Parliament.
 
• The Vice-President is also elected for a term of five years and can be re-elected.
 
• Article 69 deals with the Oath or affirmation by the Vice-President.
 
 
• Every Vice-President shall, before entering upon his office, make and subscribe before the President, or some person appointed on that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation.
 
 
 
• Article 68 deals with the Time of holding an election to fill vacancies in the office of Vice-President and the term of office of the person elected to fill the casual vacancy.

questions.question: Which article of Indian Constitution talks about Advocate-General for the State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**165**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 165** of the Indian Constitution is related to the office of **Advocate General of State**.

 
 
• He is the** highest law officer of the state.**
 
 
 
• The appointment of the Advocate General is done by the Governor on the advice of the council of ministers of the state.
 
• The person who is eligible to hold the office of advocate general in India must meet the following criteria:
 
 
• He must be an **Indian Citizen.**
 
• He should be **eligible to be appointed as the judge of the High Court**; i.e. he must meet one of the following eligibility criteria:
 
 
• A barrister having experience of more than 5 years.
 
• A civil servant with an experience of more than 10 years along with an experience as a servant in Zila Court for at least 3 years.
 
• A pleader over 10 years in any high court
 
 
 
• He **shouldn’t be more than 62 years of age**, as is the age qualification for a High Court Judge.
 
 
 
• The Constitution **does not fix the term** of Advocate General in India. He remains in the office during the pleasure of the Governor.
 
• The process and justifications for removing the Advocate General of State are not found in the Constitution. The **governor has the right to remove him or her at any time.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Duties and functions** of the **Advocate General of State**:

 
 
• When the governor directs him to counsel on legal concerns, it is his duty to advise the state government.
 
• In addition, he must carry out any legal responsibilities delegated to him by the state governor.
 
• He is obligated by the Constitution to carry out the tasks and responsibilities specified in it or in any other constitutional law.
 
 
 
• **Article 145** of Indian Constitution deals with the **Rules of Courts,** etc.
 
• **Article 77** of Indian Constitution mentions the **Conduct of business of the Government of India**.
 
• **Article 136** of Indian Constitution addresses the **special leave to appeal by the Supreme court**.
 
 
• It means that, with the exception of military tribunals and court-martials, the Supreme Court is empowered to grant, at its discretion, special leave to appeal from any judgment in any case rendered by any court or tribunal within the borders of India.
 
 
 
• Attorney General of India:
 
 
• Article 76 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment, duties, and qualifications of the Attorney General of India.
 
 
• The Attorney General of India will be appointed by the President from among those who meet the requirements to be appointed as Supreme Court judges.
 
• The Attorney General will serve as long as the President so desires.
 
 
 
• He is the chief law officer in the country.
 
 
• He provides legal advice to the Government of India and represents the Government in legal matters.
 
• He also has the power to appear in any court of law in India and can take part in any proceedings that affect the Government of India.
 
• Thus he have the right of audience in all Indian courts while carrying out his duties.
 
 
 
• Under Article 88 of the Indian Constitution, he is free to participate in and speak at any session of the Houses of Parliament, as well as in any joint session, and to be appointed to any committee of the Parliament; however, he is not entitled to vote. 
 
• He is entitled to all the privileges and immunities that are granted to members of Parliament.

questions.question: Which Turkish invader attacked and raided the temple of Somnath in 1025 AD?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahmud Ghazni.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Turkish invader **Mahmud Ghazni**, attacked and **raided **the temple of **Somnath in 1025 AD**.
 
• The first of India's twelve sacred jyotirlingas is said to have arisen at the elaborately carved honey-colored Somnath temple or Deo Patan, is located in Prabhas Patan, Veraval in Gujarat, India.
 
 
• It is said that Shiva manifested there as a blazing column of light.
 
• The temples are situated where the Sarasvati, Hiran, and Kapila rivers converge, and the shoreline where they are built is touched by the ebb and flow of the Arabian Sea.
 
• Although the timeline of the ancient temple starts in 649 BC, it is thought to be older.
 
• Though it's difficult to see them through the foggy glass, vibrant dioramas depicting the Shiva narrative border the north side of the temple grounds.
 
• The temple was reconstructed several times in the past after repeated destruction by multiple Muslim invaders and rulers, notably starting with an attack by Mahmud Ghazni in the 11th century.
 
 
• The Pran-Pratistha at the existing temple was done on 11th May 1951 by then President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muhammad Yamin ad-Dawlah** In the province of Ghazna, **Mahmud ibn** **Sebuktigin **was born on November 2, 971.

 
 
• He **founded **the **Turkic Ghaznavid dynasty,** which ruled from 998 to 1030.
 
• By the time of his death, his domain had grown into a vast military empire that included Khwarazm in Transoxiana, Punjab in India, Makran, and northwest Iran itself.
 
• Famous **Poet **Patronized by Mahmud Ghazni were **Firdausi **who wrote **Shahnameh **and **Alberuni **who wrote **Kitab-i-hind.**
 
• Mahmud **invaded Gujarat **in **1025**, plundering the **Somnath shrine **and destroying its jyotirlinga. His loot included 2 million dinars. Somnath was conquered, and Anhilwara was invaded as retaliation.
 
 
 
• **Mu'izz ad-Din Muhammad**, also called **Muhammad of Ghor**, ruled the **Ghurid Empire** as its lone ruler from **1202 to 1206**, having served as its sultan from 1173 to 1202.
 
 
• He is credited with bringing about centuries-long **Muslim hegemony on the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• Originating from Persia, Muhammad Ghori reigned over portions of what is now Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Pakistan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughluq (MBT)** was the son of Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, also known as **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**, who **founded the Tughlaq dynasty** by subduing the Delhi Sultanate. 
 
 
• Other names for him are **Ulugh Khan** and **Prince Fakhr Malik Jauna Khan**.
 
• The Deccan region of India, which is now Maharashtra, is home to **Daulatabad**, also called **Devagiri**, and it was Tughluq who **ordered the relocation of his capital from Delhi.**
 
• He introduced **token money** in the form of brass and copper coins with a par value with gold and silver coins.

questions.question: India first participated in the Olympics in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1900**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's connection to the Olympics** dates back to the **1900 Paris Olympics**, the **second modern Games**.
 
• Calcutta (now Kolkata)-born **Norman Pritchard** became the **first Indian to take part** in an Olympics.
 
 
• He **ran in five athletics events** - the 60m, the 100m, the 200m, the 110m hurdles and the 200m hurdles.
 
• India** won its first Olympic medal** - **a silver in the 200m sprint**__, as Norman Pritchard crossed the finish line behind **Walter Tewksbury **of the United States.
 
• It made **Pritchard **the **first Asian-born athlete to win an Olympic medal**.
 
 
 
• 
 
**India first** sent its **official contingent of athletes** at the **1920 Antwerp Olympics**.

 
 
• 
 
Eminent businessman **Dorabji Tata** is credited with taking the initiative to form an ‘Indian Olympic Association’ to pick and train athletes who could participate in the 1920 Olympics.

 __
 
• 
 
The first-ever Indian Olympic contingent comprised **Purma Bannerjee **(100m and 400m), **Phadeppa Chaugule** (10000m and marathon), **Sadashiv Datar** (marathon),** Kumar Navale** and **Randhir Shindes** (both wrestling).

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Indian Olympic Association **was established in the year 1927.

 
 
• It is registered as a Non-Profit Organisation under the Societies Registration Act of 1860.
 
• As a member of the IOC and OCA, it is the Indian Olympic Association’s primary mission to develop, promote and protect the Olympic Movement in the country.
 
 
 
• **Olympic Games**:
 
 
• The **first Olympic games** were reportedly staged in **Olympia in 776 BCE,** marking the Olympics' historical roots in ancient **Greece**.
 
• These ancient games were held every four years in Olympia to **honor the Greek god Zeus.**
 
• The **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** was founded in **1894**, and the **first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896**.
 
• Women competed for the first time at the 1900 Games in Paris.
 
• Women competed in every sport at the 2012 London Olympics for the first time, thanks to the addition of women's boxing to the Olympic program.
 
• The **1940 Olympics **are referred to as the **"Missing Olympics" **since they were moved to Helsinki, Finland, and eventually **abandoned due to World War II.**
 
• The Olympics have been held every four years since 1948.
 
• The **XXXII Olympics Games** were held in **Tokyo**, Japan.
 
• The **2024**, **2028 **and **2032 **Olympic Games are to be held in **Paris (France)**,** Los Angeles (USA)** and **Brisbane (Australia)** respectively.

questions.question: A settlement in closely built area of dwellings, wherever flat land is available is called _________.

__
 
• A settlement in closely built area of dwellings, wherever flat land is available is called **Compact settlement**.
 
• These settlements **develop generally in the fertile plains** and **valleys**.
 
• The **density **of population is **high **due to productive land.
 
• **Agriculture** is the **main occupation** of the people.
 
• These have **problems** **of sanitation** and **drainage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In urban planning, the **grid plan**, **grid street plan**, or **gridiron plan** is a type of city plan in which **streets run at right angles** to each other, forming a grid.
 
• A **Line settlement **or **Linear settlement **is a collection of buildings or a settlement that is created in a long line; these are often modest to medium-sized settlements.
 
 
• A lot of these **communities are built along transportation corridors** like **roads**, **rivers**, or **canals**.
 
• Others arise as a result of geographical limitations like hills, valleys, mountains, and coasts. A linear colony might not have a clear center.
 
 
 
• One of the primary categories of settlement patterns that landscape historians use to categorize rural communities in England and other countries is the **dispersed settlement**, also referred to as the **scattered settlement.**
 
 
• Usually, the region is made up of several distinct farmsteads dispersed all across it.
 
• Houses in dispersed villages are few and spaced widely apart.
 
• These kinds of villages are typically found in **high terrain regions**, **hot deserts**, grasslands, deep forests, and vast agricultural fields.

questions.question: __________ is the minimum amount of funds that the banks have to keep with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as deposits.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cash Reserve Ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
Cash reserve ratio (CRR): 

 
 
• It is **a monetary policy tool **used **by** central banks including the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, to **regulate **and control the **money supply** in the economy.
 
• **CRR **is the **percentage of total deposits that commercial banks are required to keep as reserves with the central bank**.
 
• It is a portion of the bank's demand and time liabilities.
 
• The **primary objective **of implementing CRR is to **ensure the liquidity and stability of the banking system **while controlling inflation and managing credit growth.
 
• When the **central bank** **increases the CRR**, it **reduces the amount of money available for lending by commercial banks**.
 
 
• This helps reduce excess liquidity in the economy, controlling inflationary pressures, and curbing excessive credit expansion.
 
 
 
• On the other hand, when the central bank decreases the CRR, it increases the amount of money available for lending by commercial banks.
 
• This can stimulate credit growth, promote economic activity, and ease liquidity conditions in the economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Repo Rate:

 
 
• It is the rate at which a nation's central bank lends money to commercial banks when there is a lack of funds by buying securities.
 
• In order to manage inflation, monetary authorities use repo rate.
 
• Central banks raise the repo rate in an effort to combat inflation since it discourages banks from borrowing.
 
• This eventually lowers the amount of money in circulation, which aids in containing inflation.
 
 
 
• 
 
Bank Rate:

 
 
• It is the rate at which commercial banks borrow money from the RBI without securities.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India regulates bank rates.
 
• Since it can control liquidity, it is typically higher than a repo rate.
 
 
 
• **​Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) :**
 
 
• It is a mechanism **used by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) **and other central banks to **implement monetary policy**.
 
• It **permits banks to lend money to the RBI through reverse repo agreements** or to receive money through repurchase agreements (repos).

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is India’s central bank.

 
 
• In compliance with the terms of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, it was founded on April 1, 1935 in Calcutta.

 
 
• It was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937.
 
 
 
• Though originally privately owned, since nationalisation in 1949, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India.
 
• As a qualitative instrument of monetary policy, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) employs moral suasion.
 
• It regulates the issue of Bank notes and keeping of reserves with a view to securing monetary stability in India and generally to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• It also monitors the monetary policies through its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).
